title: Born Into Black Nights

supportedRulesets.progressionRecommendation: Use native Cairn character/progression assumptions; the source does not specify a D&D-style level.
Determine equivalent low-scale undead/dungeon difficulty through the selected rules adapter; do not advertise a fixed level until conversion QA exists.
supportedRulesets.conversionNotes: Creator explicitly states the adventure can be adapted to another fantasy TTRPG with minimal adjustment.

source.title: Born Into Black Nights

playerMetadata.pitch: A small woodland town is being tormented by nightmares and restless dead. Investigate the townspeople, trace the haunting through dangerous woods, and discover what an old founder truly needs before violence makes the curse worse.

hard.rule: Kyran disturbed Bertram's tomb and stole Bertram's ring; this disturbance caused the supernatural unrest.
Bertram wants to be laid properly to rest, not to conquer or punish the town.
Fleur descends from Bertram and Zahra is especially sensitive to his unrest.
Permanent resolution requires restoring Bertram to his sarcophagus and performing a peaceful rest rite; combat victory alone is insufficient.
Complete destruction of Bertram can lead to his return about a month later as a ghost with renewed nightmares/possession threat.

conditional.rule: Zahra sleepwalks toward the ruins if allowed to leave town during an episode.
Disturbing the grave hall awakens its buried skeletons.
The town nightmare crisis ends when Bertram is properly laid to rest.

soft.rule: Minor townspeople, ordinary buildings and local services may be improvised because the source explicitly leaves Bertram's Grove open for Warden expansion.

freeImprovisation.rule: Weather, routine dialogue, incidental residents, travel colour and ordinary town services may be improvised if they do not alter clue ownership or campaign truth.

clocks.name: Nightmare Crisis
clocks.advanceRule: Advance narratively if the party abandons the town/tomb problem or worsens Bertram's unrest.
effects: Complete destructive handling can create a future ghost/possession campaign state

scenes.title: Nightmares in Bertram's Grove
requiredFacts: The town suffers recurring nightmares; Zahra is the most visible victim.

choices.label: Ask townspeople about undead in the woods
Investigate the tavern and suspicious travellers

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Resolve any town action normally. Minor residents/services may be invented, but mandatory clue ownership and ancestry/cause cannot change.

scenes.title: The Burgomaster's Household
requiredFacts: Zahra has severe nightmares and sleepwalking; Tiana is exhausted from preventing her departure.
hiddenFacts: Zahra is drawn toward the tomb because of ancestry.

choices.label: Watch Zahra during a sleepwalking episode

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Allow protective, investigative or magical approaches without prematurely revealing ancestry unless earned.

scenes.title: Osian's Memory
requiredFacts: Osian suspects the old tomb was disturbed and personally knew Bertram.
hiddenFacts: Osian knows the Bertram ancestry and can recognise the stolen ring.

choices.label: Ask about Bertram and the tomb
Show Osian suspicious objects or the ring

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Osian may reveal only source-backed historical/ancestry knowledge; do not turn him into a spell-solving deus ex machina.

scenes.title: The Grave Robber
requiredFacts: Kyran is preparing to leave and is strongly motivated by money.
hiddenFacts: Kyran disturbed the tomb and stole Bertram's ring.

choices.label: Follow Kyran instead of confronting him

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Allow any plausible social/criminal approach. Kyran can die or escape without changing the true cause; preserve another path to the tomb/rest solution.

scenes.title: Signs in the Woods
requiredFacts: Undead have been seen moving through the woods; the tomb is overgrown and easy to miss.

choices.label: Use local guidance or herb-search directions

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Use the woodland encounter table when appropriate. Creative navigation may still find the tomb if reasonably supported.

scenes.title: The Forgotten Tomb
requiredFacts: The overgrown tomb was disturbed recently relative to its long peace.
hiddenFacts: Several reinforced/blocked passages reflect Kyran's retreat through the tomb.

choices.label: Search for signs of the grave robber

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Preserve exact room topology and door state. Do not teleport characters between unconnected rooms.

scenes.title: Among the Restless Dead
requiredFacts: Room-specific hazards trigger from player actions and local conditions; wandering monsters remain possible.
hiddenFacts: The tomb contains historical/religious context showing it was meant for peaceful rest.

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Run the actual room entered from locations.md/encounters.md. The listed choices are navigation suggestions, not a skip over unexplored topology.

scenes.title: Bertram's Rest
requiredFacts: Bertram manifests as a Draugr with skeletons; his remains and sarcophagus are here.
hiddenFacts: Defeating him is not the permanent solution.

choices.label: Defeat the Draugr and investigate the sarcophagus
Try to understand what the restless dead need
Use Bertram's ring/journal or funerary clues

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Resolve combat/social/ritual improvisation honestly. Bertram's incoherent Draugr state cannot provide a convenient exposition monologue. Clues and ritual logic must come from established evidence/actions.

scenes.title: Lay the Founder to Rest
requiredFacts: A peaceful restoration of Bertram's remains is required for permanent resolution.

choices.label: Return Bertram to the sarcophagus, restore the ring if available, close it and offer peaceful rites

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Accept equivalent sincere peaceful-rest actions. The stolen ring helps but is not an absolute completion lock if unavailable.

scenes.title: Quiet Graves
requiredFacts: The undead return to rest and the nightmare crisis ends.

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Allow epilogue/free play in town; no further forced campaign choice is required.

scenes.title: The Dead Stir Again
requiredFacts: Combat alone does not permanently end the haunting.

choices.label: Seek another way to learn the burial rite

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Continue the unresolved campaign without falsely awarding permanent victory.

scenes.title: A Worse Ghost
requiredFacts: Complete destruction can cause Bertram to return in roughly a month as a ghost, with nightmares and possession risk.

freeTextPolicy.adjudicationRule: Treat this as a delayed-failure campaign continuation state rather than an immediate clean victory.

endings.title: Bertram Properly Laid to Rest
endings.summary: The tomb quiets, its undead return to their graves and the nightmares end. Oskar/town rewards and possible homestead follow.

endings.title: Undead Defeated, Haunting Unresolved
endings.summary: The party wins a fight but not the campaign problem; the dead begin to return and nightmares persist.

endings.title: Bertram Destroyed
endings.summary: The body is destroyed, but the source establishes a later ghost return with renewed nightmares and possession risk.

endings.title: Bertram's Grove Abandoned
endings.summary: The nightmare crisis remains active. DMOS preserves the unresolved state for later return rather than forcing off-screen resolution.

adaptationNotes: Do not create a D&D level range without separate conversion QA.
The ring is a powerful clue/restoration component but the source does not make it an absolute hard gate if unavailable.
Town expansion is explicitly allowed; generated townspeople must not replace named clue holders.
Visual map ingestion is useful but non-blocking because room connection/door-state information is present in source text.
